entries.title: Verify the published scope and technical limits of bad_query
entries.claim: The upstream project documents a sandbox-escape proof of concept whose stated OS range overlaps iOS 26.6.1.
entries.expected_observation: Primary source code and documentation identify the mechanism, prerequisites, limitations, and exact supported builds.
entries.falsifying_observation: The source does not support the stated version range, prerequisites are unmet, or no verifiable technical evidence backs the claim.
prerequisites: Review source and license without executing the project
Separate documentation claims from behavior established by code

entries.title: Determine which customizations Erosion actually permits
entries.claim: Erosion documents limited customization capabilities on some iOS 26 versions.
entries.expected_observation: Source review identifies the features, required privileges, signing/distribution model, and device/version limitations.
entries.falsifying_observation: The feature list cannot be traced to code or its prerequisites exclude the target.
prerequisites: Review source, dependencies, license, and distribution method
Do not install or execute binaries during initial review

entries.title: Separate documented app-data access from full jailbreak capability
entries.claim: EscapeOS documents selected app-data browsing and backup behavior, which is narrower than a full jailbreak.
entries.expected_observation: Source review maps each user-visible operation to its required access and records the devices/builds explicitly tested upstream.
entries.falsifying_observation: The source does not substantiate the documented behavior or the target prerequisites differ materially.
prerequisites: Check whether host pairing or another computer is required
Do not assume a different iPhone/build test applies to iPhone17,4 / 23G83

warning: These entries are research questions, not proof of exploitability or a working jailbreak.
